Meanwhile a user who selects CR129's **Day Trader** preset is self-identifying as exactly the cohort the research is about, and we have nothing addressed to them: the existing curriculum teaches the concepts (**047** revenge trading, **051** discipline, **012** why most traders fail) but speaks to a swing/position trader throughout. **Editorial stance, decided before any writing — NOT abstinence.** A track arguing "don't day trade" is dismissed by its own audience in lesson one and teaches nothing; per Saiful, *"if we do not let them fail in a safe environment, they will fail with real money."* The evidence does not say never — it says this is brutally hard, <1% sustain it, here is what separates them, and here is how to find out which group you are in **while it is still free**. The honest frame is that **AMI is the cheapest possible place to discover you are not in the 1%**, which is a real service and needs no flattering of the odds. **Proposed six** (shape, not mandate): (1) what the data actually says, without editorial; (2) why activity costs you *before* costs — 11.4% vs 18.5% with equal stock-picking; (3) overconfidence as the mechanism, and the disposition effect; (4) the tilt spiral measured, extending 047 to intraday; (5) what the surviving 1% do differently — falsifiable habits, not mindset talk (Cross-Section of Speculator Skill); (6) **running the experiment on yourself** using the CR129 preset plus CR131's outcome comparison — lesson 6 is the one that must exist, because it closes the loop between preset, evidence and the user's own results. **Hard requirements:** every numeric claim carries a frontmatter `sources:` entry (internal-only provenance, standing BOK rule) — no number without a citation, because this is the CR that most invites confident-sounding invention and this project has already been bitten by numbers arriving in a citation they had not earned; house format modelled on `047_revenge_trading.en.mdx` and `365_your_risk_limits_in_ami.en.mdx`; prerequisites chaining into 009/014/017/047/365; and the analyst-to-analyst voice — the reader has already decided to day-trade, so treat them as a colleague testing a hypothesis, not a patient to be talked down. **Also owed and tracked here so it is not lost between CRs:** lesson **047 now contains a false statement** — it says the cooldown is *"tracked in the Decision Journal, not enforced by the app,"* which CR129 makes untrue; that line must change and carries `retranslate:[ar,ms]`. **DEPENDS-ON CR129** (the limits the track explains) and **CR131** (lesson 6 links to it); lessons 1–5 can be written before either lands. | CR133 | 2026-07-30 | **[HIGH PRIORITY — Saiful, 2026-07-30]** **Bottom-nav restructure: GAME takes slot 3, `YOU` takes slot 5, Settings comes off the bar.** CR109 needs a nav slot and `hex_bottom_nav.dart` holds five, so Saiful's call was to demote Settings — *"consider moving settings to a less prominent real estate."* Three structures were on the table; **he chose the nav-survey artifact's**, then revised it: runs and trophies go back inside GAME (where CR109 §9.0 put the career record — *"career points are the game's high score, not a general account attribute"*), and slot 5 becomes **`YOU`**. **Supersedes CR109 §9.0.** Two premises in the earlier proposals do not survive the code and are recorded so they are not re-proposed: **there is no app bar to put a gear in** — 7 `AppBar(`s exist, every one on a *pushed* screen, while each of the five tabs rolls its own private `_Header` and **Floor has none at all** (its logo row sits inside a `SingleChildScrollView` and scrolls away); and **a pure career/profile tab is empty on day one** — anonymous-first onboarding, Amendment A deletes badges and streaks, so a new user sees zero runs and zero career points in prime real estate, which is the same defect the survey rejected the avatar pattern for. **The dangerous part is not the gear, it is the renumbering.** GAME lands on index 2 and inherits everything that pointed at the Journal: `portfolio_screen.dart:1528` (`state = 2, // Journal`) makes Portfolio History's **"Review in Journal" open the game**, and `journal_screen.dart:96` (`next != 2`) fires the **Journal's coach-mark tour on the game tab**, once, then marks it seen forever. Three of the five index literals (`floor:67,320`, `portfolio:123`, `lessons:79`) keep working, **so a smoke test passes** — the DEF190 class exactly. Fix ships in phase 1 *before* any reorder: `enum AmiTab { floor, portfolio, game, lessons, you }`, `activeTabIndexProvider` → `activeTabProvider` typed on it, turning every site into a compile error; `flutter analyze` clean is the proof, and CR109's later insert of `game` becomes one line instead of a renumbering. Deep links need *tab + segment*, so the provider takes an intent, not a bare tab; and `TourSection.journal` needs a new trigger since the Journal is no longer a tab. **`YOU` takes CR120's shape** — pinned card over segmented tabs, second use of a decided idiom — holding **MANDATE** (Settings sections 1–3 lifted whole; the header already carries the mandate version and Save, so Settings *is* a mandate editor with settings appended), **JOURNAL** (moved in whole), **INSIGHTS**, and the ⚙. The mandate leaves Settings because it is a *training instrument the curriculum tells users to revisit*, not configuration; it keeps its in-context deep links from Portfolio and Lessons. INSIGHTS is the one genuinely new surface — what your decisions look like in aggregate; rejected alternatives were credits/membership (billing — behind the gear), agents-unlocked (the Floor's whole job) and streaks (Amendment A deletes them). **§4.1 exists because the first draft overclaimed and the schema check caught it: two of the five panels are NOT computable, and are recorded rather than quietly rendered as zeros.** **§4.1 now specifies five cards, each rendered full-size in the prototype's §07 build reference with its query, source line, empty state and edge case** — the reference renders the *same* component the phone does, so spec and screen cannot drift (DEF098). All five need no new table and no migration: **how your trades ended** (`SIM_TRADE` where `'closed' in tags`, bucketed on `won`/`lost`/`manual` — `sim.py:395,448`), **what PM decided** (`ROOM_RUN` grouped by `payload.verdict.action` over APPROVE/MODIFY/REJECT/PASS/NO_VERDICT — `room_runner.py:1610`), **analysts you sought out** (`ONE_ON_ONE`/`AGENT_COACH`/`AGENT_UNLOCK`, `agents_involved[0]`), **how your mandate has moved** (`MANDATE_EDIT` diffing `payload.before` vs `payload.after` — `mandate.py:147,259`), and **daily challenge by type** (`DAILY_CHALLENGE` grouped by `payload.type` — `daily_challenge.py:223`). Two findings changed the design: **"how your trades ended" is the strongest card and the cheapest** — a user who closes by hand before stop or target is overriding the plan they wrote, which is a habit and habits are what the product exists to change, and the tags already distinguish it; and **`MANDATE_EDIT` stores full before/after mandate snapshots**, so every limit's trajectory — including whether one loosened right after a loss — is reconstructable with no new table. Edge cases written into acceptance: **`NO_VERDICT` is not a rejection** (CR098 — the PM declining to rule because the run had no market read; folding it into REJECT tells the user their idea was turned down when it was never judged, and that exact mis-render is already a flagged defect elsewhere), `payload.verdict == null` on failed/cancelled runs must be excluded rather than counted as PASS, the **Day Trader preset** sets seven limits in one edit so it renders as one event not seven loosenings, a trade closed manually *at* the target still tags `manual` (correctly — the user acted, not the level), and challenge rows carry `difficulty` so an unweighted comparison must say so. Each card has an empty-state threshold rather than a degenerate ratio (trades hidden under 3 closes, challenge rows omitted under 5 attempts, drift hidden at one version) because a `1/1` bar reading 100% is the failure mode. **Measured: the assembled segment is 3.4 screens of scroll at 390×844** — the deepest in the app, acceptable only because it is read through rather than scanned; a sixth card means one comes out. **Dead enum found on the way through: `EntryType.DRIFT_ALERT` (`schemas/journal.py:31`) has no writer anywhere** — no capture site produces one — and it is the natural home for "your mandate loosened right after a loss"; flagged for the Architect, not claimed here. Not computable: **"voices you actually read" from Room runs is a wrong number** — `room_runner.py:1603` writes *every* agent in the transcript and all 12 speak every run, so the chart would report participation and label it readership (hence the re-sourcing above); **followed-PM vs overrode** has no run→trade link (`reference_id` holds the run on one entry, the trade on the other) and costs one line to stamp `from_run_id` into the SIM_TRADE payload, which is already JSON so no migration; and **safety-floor stops** are absent entirely because journal capture at `sim.py:307` runs only after `result.trade is not None` and a blocked trade has no trade — **the app never records that it stopped you**, which for a training product is the teaching moment going unlogged and is worth its own item regardless of this CR. Acceptance adds: INSIGHTS renders no figure it cannot derive, and never as `0` (CR040). Bars are coloured by **family** (cyan Analysts, amber Risk, purple Research, green Execution), never by member — four analysts sharing one cyan is correct. **New hazard the layout creates, designed against explicitly:** the mandate has a dirty state and an explicit Save, so switching segments mid-edit is silent data loss — Save stays pinned, a dirty marker shows on the segment, and the switch must prompt (CR040: fail visibly). **Two shipped strings name a screen by its position in the nav**, and one fires at the worst possible moment: `app_en.arb:1121` `tradeTicketChangeMandate` — *"Change what is enforced via Settings → My Mandate"* — renders on the trade ticket **when a compliance breach has just blocked the trade** (`trade_ticket_sheet.dart:416`, inside the violations block after the Sharia banner); `app_en.arb:85` `floorRestartOnboardingConfirmBody` repeats it. **The obvious fix — rename the path to "YOU → Mandate" — was rejected.** Saiful: *"always make it easier for the user!"* A rename leaves the same trap armed for the next nav change and still makes the user walk there. **Replace the instruction with the control:** the blocked ticket becomes *"Change what is enforced."* + an **`OPEN MY MANDATE`** button that pushes the mandate directly — one tap from the block to the rule that caused it — and the restart dialog simply drops the path (*"that stays as it is, and you can edit it any time"*) with **no** button, since a third action navigating away from a two-action confirm is worse, not easier. Not a new pattern: `floorLockedGoToLessons` (`app_en.arb:101`) already ships as **"GO TO LESSONS"**, a button rather than directions. `retranslate:[ar,ms]` on both; `safety_floor.md:182,190` has the PM *say* the path — worse than a label, since it reads as AMI's own reasoning — flagged for the agents track (not in shipped `.py`). **Plus a guard, because this string has already been wrong once:** `@floorRestartOnboardingConfirmBody`'s own metadata records **DEF158** correcting it for claiming a data loss that never happened — same string, same confident-wrongness class — and nothing couples `app_en.arb` to `home_shell.dart`, so `mobile/test/l10n_key_parity_test.dart` (which already walks every ARB) gains one rule: **no message value may name a nav destination followed by `→`**. Verified safe against today's file — the remaining arrows are CTAs (*"Next →"*, *"Try it now →"*, *"Tap to attempt →"*, *"Include the {agent} →"*) and the label *"RISK → REWARD"*; only the two offenders hit. Also extracts one `AmiScreenHeader` from the four private `_Header`s (DEF098 class — adding a fifth by hand is how it stays that way). **Separately flagged for the Architect to mint as its own DEF:** the only way to file a bug report is Settings → scroll past 13 sections → **long-press an unlabelled grey version string** (`settings_screen.dart:249`, `_AppVersionChip` at `:1139`), while `bug_report_sheet.dart:5` documents *"call this from anywhere"* and exactly one caller exists — already broken, and demoting Settings makes the alpha feedback channel worse. **Phase 1 needs nothing from the backend and does not wait for the game**: it ships at **four tabs** (`FLOOR · PORTFOLIO · LESSONS · YOU`) — no placeholder cell, because the Journal isn't missing, it moved inside `YOU`, and an empty "coming soon" tab is a promise in prime real estate. Measured in the prototype at 390pt: five cells give 77.6pt each with `PORTFOLIO` rendering at 52.4pt, four give 97.0pt, so DEF043 does not recur at either count — checked by rendered size, not line count, since `FittedBox(scaleDown)` hides a wrap by shrinking type. Spec + clickable prototype delivered, **no Flutter written**. | CR134 | 2026-07-30 | **CR109's game screens checked against the design system — 27 findings, and the guard for why nobody caught them.** Saiful: *"look at CR109 and look at the UI designs. make sure they adhere to the rest of the application designs."* The designs exist — AT:Gamer's artifact carries **20 mocked screens in journey order**, and they are careful work: tokens verbatim from `ami_theme.dart`, the type ramp correctly scaled (`.big` 33px = `statBig` 42 × 0.79 at the 310px frame), `tabular-nums` everywhere, dark-only correctly observed (D-062), the heat gauge correctly a bar rather than a ring, and **screen 18 the best degrade-loudly design in the product**. **What is absent is the design system.** The whole CR109 package — 13 documents, 5,297 lines — references it **exactly once**, in `lane_drafts/CR109-1-MOBILE.assign.draft.md:30`, and that one line is also the one that hands a coder a forbidden encoding. §19's ~60 acceptance criteria are exhaustive on scoring, integrity, restart, fees and feature cross-products and contain **no design criterion of any kind**. **The single hardest fact: zero hexagons in twenty screens** — `grep -c "clip-path"` and `grep -c "polygon("` both return 0, so every chip, tab, size-chip, nav cell and button is a rounded rect, in an app whose design language is named Hex-Reinforced Precision and whose rule (`ami_hex_in_flutter.md:189`, pinned in `cta_shape_test.dart`) is *"hex geometry is for marks and controls."* Findings, grouped: **provenance** — the equity curve draws one solid path and never renders `price_source`, which is the entire reason it is on the wire; the counterfactual *"if you'd just held the S&P +0.61%"* is a simulation drawn as a measurement on the highest-attention screen in the product; the wildness index composites concentration, position count, turnover and volatility with **no stated weighting**, which `data_viz:73` forbids outright; returns-by-style has no small-n floor, so `1 of 1` reads 100%. **Colour** — every primary CTA is cyan, which is the four Analysts, where `colors_motion_rtl.md:28` says hex-blue *regardless of context*; the career title `Analyst` renders **purple on screen 00 and cyan on screen 19**, inconsistent with itself and unresolvable against the Analyst family mark either way; §13.3 says to reuse `league_common.dart` for exactly this, whose `leagueTierColor()` maps tiers onto four family hues and whose only two importers are **on §13.4's own deletion list** — CR109 orphans it one paragraph after recommending it. **§8.3's champion skin recolours agent frames amber**, and amber is simultaneously the three Risk debators' family colour and the app's attention state (`HexAvatarStatus.attention` is an amber pulse; `room_screen.dart:712,793` are amber warning cards), so a champion's Room reads as twelve agents flagging a problem; the idea and its economics are right and only the channel is wrong — champion status is *hierarchy*, and `data_viz:43` gives hierarchy to **stroke weight**, so a 2px frame in each agent's own family colour plus §8.3's own Room plaque keeps every hue, stays zero-art and still reads instantly. **The mirrors render as verdicts** — §10.4 insists three times that they are *"measurement instead of guardrails,"* *"not a rule, not a warning, no gate,"* *"never scolds"*, and then book heat ships as an amber bar with an amber `High` chip, returns-by-style as red on *wild* and green on *disciplined*, and the modeled trading cost in amber: **colour is what turns a mirror into a scold**, whatever the copy says. Two ambers land on one confirm card, which `room_board.dart:53` carries a shipped comment forbidding (*"two different amber things on one card is one too many"*), and amber on a *modeled* cost breaks `data_viz:64` directly (*"derived ≠ dangerous… never amber — a system-supplied default is not a risk, it is a different kind of fact"*), which also catches the amber MOCK days on screen 18. **One finding has a clock on it:** `CR109-1-MOBILE.assign.draft.md:34` offers *"a dashed segment, **a muted colour**, or a flagged tick, your call"* for marking non-live price points — `data_viz:44` puts opacity/saturation ramps in the forbidden row outright (*"a dimmed mark reads as **absent**, not **small**"*) and `:64` pins provenance to fill-vs-outline plus a dashed segment. **That lane is drafted and waiting to be lifted**, so the fix is written out verbatim in the review for the Gamer track to paste; CR109's own files are not touched here (CR081 sweep risk on a shared checkout). **Motion, decided by Saiful this session:** §10.2's *"the curve replayed"* against `data_viz:257` (*"marks must not fly into position, counters must not tick up"*). He chose the bounded exception — **one draw-on, ≤600ms, `easeOut`, removed under `disableAnimations`, ceremony surfaces only**; 600ms is not a new number, it is what `HexBurstOverlay` has shipped since CR004, so this documents an exception the app already has. **The `+112 pts` delta is stamped and never counts up** — *no motion on text* stands unamended. Written into `data_viz_and_meters.md` **§7.1** as a named, bounded carve-out rather than left as a precedent. Also amended **§4.1**, which specced the KPI tile as a `CutCornerOctagonClipper(cornerCut: 10)` panel while §4.0 said surfaces are rounded rects and **all four shipped implementations are rounded-rect or unclipped** — a spec describing a component nothing implements, found because CR109 §13.3 is the first change that has to extract it. Remaining findings: RTL exists in the package only as *"Arabic is RTL"* for strings while the game is wall-to-wall numeric pairs and CR106 **measured** `2.8 : 1` rendering as `1 : 2.8` unisolated; nav icons are U+25xx codepoints absent from both the bundled subset and Inter, the class that turned a caret into a full stop in the CR120 prototype; `Celebrate.major` cannot be generalised as §13.3 asks (it is `major(ctx, {required Agent agent})` pushing `AgentUnlockedScreen`, docstring *"agent unlock only"*); the settlement freeze re-invents the Room's `withheld_tenure` card, which already carries the rule *"purple, not amber, so the card never LOOKS like the credits-withheld state"*; the reuse list omits `AmiEmptyState` despite ≥6 empty states including *"the empty book — must not be a blank list"*; 20 new surfaces join none of `screen_inventory.md`; and the artifact's nav is stale against CR133's decided `FLOOR · PORTFOLIO · GAME · LESSONS · YOU`. **The guard, because this is a second occurrence:** CR106 §4.0 records the first — the hex rule lived only in a decision record and `HexButton` shipped wrong for months. CR113's remedy was to move the rule where its audience reads, which was right and insufficient: relocating a rule improves the odds someone consults it and does nothing when the author never asks. Filed as **`failure_patterns.md` P14 — a spec governed by a system that references it zero times**, the inversion of P11 (a rule *stated* once and *enforced* nowhere, which no sweep finds because the offending document contains no instance of the thing). Its invariant: *a spec producing user-visible surfaces is not complete until its acceptance criteria include the design system as assertions* — because a CR's acceptance list is its real specification and anything absent from it is optional in practice. §3 of the review is the first worked instance: shape, colour, honesty, mirror-neutrality, motion and bidi criteria phrased so `cta_shape_test.dart` or a widget test can assert them, for the Architect to fold into CR109 §19. Deliverables: the review in CR109's folder (a new file, disjoint write path, matching that folder's `*_review.md` convention) and a prototype rendering **six screens as drawn beside the same six corrected** at **exactly 390pt viewports** — measured, not asserted: `PORTFOLIO` renders 52.2pt in a 78.0pt cell, matching CR133's 52.4pt, so DEF043 does not recur. Clip geometry is transcribed from `hex_clipper.dart` rather than approximated, and every hex literal inside the phone frames resolves to an `AmiColors` token except the one being criticised. **Layout, copy and hierarchy are CR109's throughout — a conformance pass, not a redesign.
